findings.title: _current_weather books forecast row 0's wind as current at any age; the N-no-expiry barrier cannot see an index-0 read
findings.claim: During a weather-fetch outage of 1 to 72 h, HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._current_weather returns the wind of the held forecast's first row, not the row covering now (or none past the horizon), at all 72 of 72 hours. At 30 h the diagnosis record books 10.0 m/s where the covering row says 40.0. The fixed sibling forecast_outdoor_now, over the same rows, mismatches at 0 of 72 hours.
findings.mechanism: _current_weather reads self._weather_forecast[0] with no timestamp match and no end bound. The forecast is kept verbatim when a fetch fails or returns empty: _fetch_weather keeps the previous list and only marks _weather_stale_since, and no learner freezes on that. So once the source stops updating, the row booked as 'now' drifts back by the outage length. It feeds the house and lower-floor loss replay (_replay_interval -> _replay_step's weather argument) and the #52 diagnosis capture's planned.wind_speed. forecast_outdoor_now's own docstring names this exact assumption as wrong ('Assuming entry 0 is the current hour ... a stale forecast ... reads hours out of phase'), and #2229 fixed that sibling with _covering_index. findings.title: prepr.sh --self-test evals an unterminated step-1a3 block: every run prints a bash syntax error and its null pin passes through it
findings.claim: The self-test's step-1a3 extraction (sed from '# --- 1a3.' to '# --- 1b0.') now ends inside the open `if [ -n "$REUSE" ]; then ... else` that was inserted before 1b0, so the null-control arm's eval raises 1 bash syntax error on every run (the 'eval: syntax error: unexpected end of file' tail of each prepr.sh --self-test), and the pin 'step 1a3 lets a body naming this head run every step' passes on output produced after the parse failure.
findings.mechanism: bash's eval runs complete top-level commands as it parses them, so the leading 1a3 `if` executes (the refuse arm exits 1 inside it, the null arm falls past it), then the parser meets the unterminated REUSE `if` and aborts the eval; `echo FELL-THROUGH` after the eval prints regardless. The null pin keys on FELL-THROUGH alone, never on the eval's status or stderr, so it cannot tell 'the arm let the body through' from 'the eval died'. The block also carries the PREPR_RECORDER_CACHE line, so the self-test writes a stray /tmp/prepr-recpy.<pid>. The pins still pass (rc 0), so the defect is silent: the barrier's drive is no longer the code it says it drives.

findings.title: N-reap-lock: an entry unload cancels its refresh but not the solve, so the reloaded entry's first solve waits out every orphan
findings.claim: When an entry is unloaded (an options save reloads it) while a solve is in flight, async_shutdown cancels the refresh task awaiting coordinator._await_process but the executor thread keeps running _run_in_process under _PROCESS_LOCK, and nothing on the unload path reaps the worker, so the new entry's first job waits out the orphan's remaining time (ratio 1.00) and, after three reloads, out three whole orphaned solves (17.0 s behind 6 s jobs, 2.83x one job).
findings.mechanism: Teardown ordered behind the lock a solve holds, on the unload seam: the stop path (_shutdown_process_pool, HA stop only) kills first and bounds its lock wait to 5 s (guarded, 0.00 s measured), but async_unload_entry -> async_shutdown only cancels the asyncio side; run_in_executor cannot cancel a started thread, and each orphan job still queued on _PROCESS_LOCK runs its full solve after acquiring it, its result discarded.

evidence.unit: s wall for a 0 s job submitted after 3 cancelled 6 s refreshes (reload3_first_job_wall_s); single reload 5.00 s = 1.00 x the orphan's remaining time

evidence.contention_note: provisional: two other finder seats on the box (load1 ~9); the jobs are time.sleep in the real worker, so the wall is set by the job length, not by CPU contention
